### Observed differences

- Two activities appear only in the later window: A01 runs in about 28 in 100 traces (55 of 200) and A02 in about 39 in 100 (78 of 200); neither was observed in the earlier window. [OCC001, OCC002]
- A14 is no longer observed: it ran in about 26 in 100 traces before (51 of 200, occasionally repeated within a trace), and in none afterwards; its co-occurrences with A12 and with A13 (about 26 in 100 traces each before) also vanish. [OCC007, POS002, REL021, REL022]
- In the later window, A12 leads directly to A03, whereas before A12 was always followed by A14 and A14 by A03; the A12→A03 distance within five steps shortens from typically two steps to one. [DIR003, DIR004, LAG003]
- In the later window, A03's route to A13 goes via A02: before, A03's outgoing transitions split about evenly between A12 (about 51%) and A13 directly (about 49%); after, A03 leads to A02 in about 54% of its outgoing transitions and to A12 in about 46%, A02 always leads to A13, and A02 precedes A13 in about 39 in 100 traces. The A03→A13 distance shifts from directly adjacent to typically two steps. [DIR001, DIR002, REL006, LAG002]
- Both main branches run in fewer traces. Before, every trace contained exactly one of A03 (about 50 in 100) or A07 (about 50 in 100), and A13 (about 50 in 100) always accompanied A03; in the later window A03 and A02 occur together in about 39 in 100 traces, the A07 side in about 34 in 100, and about 28 in 100 traces contain neither. A05, A07, A09, A10 and A11 each fall from about 50 to about 34 in 100 traces, and A13 from about 50 to about 39. [REL008, REL013, REL001, OCC003, OCC004, OCC005, OCC006, REL015, REL018]
- Self-repetition distances shrink: A03→A03 and A12→A12 repetitions move from typically three steps apart to typically two, consistent with the loop no longer passing through A14. [LAG001, LAG004]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the hypothesis that the control flow around A03 was restructured. In the earlier window, A12 was always followed by A14 and A14 by A03, closing a loop back to A03, and A03 led directly to A13 in about half of its outgoing transitions; in the later window, A12 leads directly back to A03 while A14 is no longer observed, and a new activity A02 sits between A03 and A13 — A03 leads to A02, A02 always leads to A13, and A02 occurs only in traces that also contain A03. A01 also appears as a new activity in about 28 in 100 traces, though the evidence contains no relational items for it, so where it fits remains unknown. [DIR003, DIR004, LAG003, DIR001, DIR002, REL006, REL001, OCC007, OCC002, OCC001]

The screening context makes sampling noise an unlikely explanation for the pattern as a whole: 40 items qualified where roughly 0.32 would be expected without change, every item's difference exceeds about 995 of 1000 random re-splits, and the structural claim rests on directly observed successor changes (A12: to A14 before, to A03 after; A03: gained A02, lost A13), corroborating lag shifts and the coherent disappearance of every A14 relation. [DIR003, DIR002, LAG003, LAG002, LAG001, LAG004, REL021, REL022]

The evidence cannot exclude that A14 remains part of the process but was skipped in all 200 later traces — zero participation only means it was not observed — nor can it show whether the rewiring around A12, the placement of A02 and the appearance of A01 stem from one modification or from separate ones. [OCC007, OCC002, OCC001]

Other differences: the branch around A07 runs less often — A05, A07, A09, A10 and A11 each drop from about 50 to about 34 in 100 traces, A12 from about 26 to about 18, and about 28 in 100 later traces contain neither main branch (before: none); the evidence cannot decide whether this is an independent shift in how often the branches are taken or a consequence of the restructuring around A03. [OCC003, OCC004, OCC005, OCC006, REL012, REL015, REL018, REL008, REL013]
